title: Carpet Age-Band Depreciation Conventions on the Security Deposit Account
content:
**Q. How does a carpet's age affect the depreciation of a carpet replacement charge on a Security Deposit Account?**
A. The carpet's age band sets the depreciation convention of its remaining share. The band is the carpet's age recorded on the carpet line, taken as a share of the carpet life.

- **Declining convention.** A carpet whose recorded age is at least 0.75 of the carpet life has a remaining share equal to the straight-line remaining share multiplied by itself.
- **Whole-year convention.** A carpet whose age is at least 0.50 but less than 0.75 of that life has its age rounded up to a whole multiple of 12 months before the straight-line remaining share is taken. An age already on a whole multiple stays as it is.
- **Straight line.** A younger carpet keeps its straight-line remaining share on its recorded age in months.

The straight-line remaining share is the carpet life less the age, never below 0, divided by the carpet life.

**Q. Which records are read?**
A. The age in months recorded on the carpet replacement line, and the carpet life of that carpet.

### Worked table (hypothetical 60-month carpet life)

| Recorded age | Share of life | Convention | Remaining share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45 | 0.75 | declining | 15 over 60 is 0.25; times itself, 0.0625 |
| 44 | 0.7333... | whole-year: age 48 | 12 over 60 is 0.2 |
| 36 | 0.6 | whole-year: 36 stays | 24 over 60 is 0.4 |
| 30 | 0.5 | whole-year: age 36 | 24 over 60 is 0.4 |
| 29 | 0.4833... | straight line | 31 over 60 is 0.51666... |
| 70 | above 1 | declining | 0 times itself, 0 |

**Q. How does the whole-year convention read on a shorter carpet life?**
A. The band is always measured against the carpet life of that carpet. On a hypothetical 50-month life, an age of 25 months is 0.50 of the life, which is the whole-year band. The age rounds up to 36 months, and the remaining share is 14 over 50, which is 0.28.
